overview: Luba political life joined sacred kingship with council authority. Artworks could carry political knowledge, embody ancestral relationships, or serve highly practical purposes within elite daily life.

items.text: Lukasa boards use carved forms or attached beads and shells to organize histories, genealogies and significant places. Their interpretation depends on trained specialists.
The mbudye association includes women and men who interpret political principles and can restrain or reinforce chiefly authority.
Female figures on royal seats, staffs and other court objects relate to ancestral kings and the sacred character of rule.
Carved headrests protected elaborate hairstyles while their owners slept. A nineteenth-century example repeats the hairstyle in the sculpture itself.
A headrest can create a strong sculptural composition with slender limbs and open spaces while still supporting the sleeper's head.

sources.title: The Met: Kingdoms of the Savanna: The Luba and Lunda Empires
